archive_work.reason: All five progress_status fields are NOT_ENABLED; no archive read/reuse counters recorded.

boundaries: All five runs bind the exact same reported signed corpus, genesis, initial root and domain, with 64 observed candidate blocks of 1024 rows and 8192 in flight.
Unlike the continuous group, all 65536 signatures and APFL preparation finish before the first timed submission. Keep these denominators and scores separate.
Only the node binary differs before/after (861 to F286); CPU business backend, AOEM, signature scheme, original four-node receipt endpoint and recovery checks are unchanged.

CPU improvement is 1.69 percent versus before and 1.19 percent versus before-repeat in this one sequence, not a repeated candidate distribution. GPU TPS improves in this sample but P99 worsens 84676 us (about 2.14 percent); not all latency metrics improve.
This does not erase the earlier 4K CPU regression or the prior 17.325802-second P99 negative, and does not establish stable performance closure or restoration of 12K.
The temporarily modified active source used for a later counterexample is outside this frozen archive-only result. No later hash/progress propagation is qualified.

limits: This is the frozen archive-only intermediate candidate. No claim applies to the later unbuilt worktree changes.
Correctness coalescing regression is demonstrated; 4K CPU regression remains about 33 percent despite the GPU sample improving.
Headline endpoint remains the slowest of four unique receipt-query observations, not internal QC, ACK, or publication time. No slow sample is removed and no denominator time is subtracted.
65K uses 8192 in flight, 1024 rows per frame and 64 observed 1024-row candidate blocks. Post-first-submit signing/preparation remain inside one uninterrupted wall.
All eight rounds passed fee-state/cold recovery and reported zero transport failures, business failures, nonce rejection and deadline expiry. These are scoped observations, not release acceptance.
No archive_work progress counters or per-object recovery event timeline were collected in these performance groups. Cannot quantify their actual archive read savings from these JSONs.
Physical wire bytes, retransmissions and peak memory are unmeasured. Logical input/application byte counts must not be relabeled as physical traffic.

This 65K group differs in genesis/input from the unchanged-binary postcleanup baseline and earlier lowdisk group. Do not ascribe cross-group differences solely to this patch or disk cleanup; prior P99 17.325802-second negative remains open.
All tests are Windows on one host with four processes; not four physical machines, Linux packaging, complete CI, or production launch. 12K is not restored and is not the ultimate ceiling.
